title: Transit routing heuristics scratchpad
content:
Context: mid-day spike on 2026-03-05 where a subset of traffic from us-east-1 experienced sudden latency jumps (200ms -> 900ms p95) and sporadic 502/504s. Smart routing policy should route to nearest healthy pool, but we observed a steady stream being routed to eu-west-1 for ~7 minutes despite local capacity availability. This doc is my scratchpad for commands, raw snippets, and hypotheses while iterating on reproducer and mitigation.

High-level timeline (rough):
- 14:02 UTC: first alerts (p95 latency + error rate) for /v1/generate on hosted-api-prod-us-east-1
- 14:05 UTC: automated fallback policy activates for ~3% of requests (observed in route-decision logs)
- 14:07-14:14 UTC: manual scaling triggered on us-east pools (capacity up by ~20%)
- 14:09 UTC: traffic still being routed to eu-west-1; error rate for routed-to-eu increases
- 14:15 UTC: temporary policy override rolled (force-local) -> error rate dropped, latency p95 improved

What I ran (commands and raw snippets):
- Inspecting route decisions (raw):
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    "https://api.redwood-internal/v1/route-decisions?start=2026-03-05T13:58:00Z&end=2026-03-05T14:20:00Z&policy=smart-routing" | jq '.items[] | {ts, request_id, client_region, selected_pool, reason_codes, metrics_snapshot}'

  Sample line from above: 
  {
    "ts": "2026-03-05T14:06:29.231Z",
    "request_id": "req_01FGX2X9T3",
    "client_region": "us-east-1",
    "selected_pool": "eu-west-1-pool-a",
    "reason_codes": ["pref_routing_unavailable","ttl_recompute"],
    "metrics_snapshot": {"pool_load_pct": 0.37}
  }

  NOTE: metrics_snapshot values in route-decision log appear stale relative to pool metrics (see below).
